**The OpenPlanner build can fail without recording a revision.**

The step uses `set -euo pipefail`. A failed `install` or `build` command therefore exits before line 124 runs. When that happens, `metadata/openplanner-revision.txt` is never written. A failed sandbox bundle is the case where the actual checked-out revision is most useful for diagnosis. The manifest also records only `OPENPLANNER_REF`, which is the requested pin and not the observed `HEAD`. Write the revision first.

<details>
<summary>Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
         run: |
           set -euo pipefail
+          git -C .sandbox-deps/openplanner rev-parse HEAD > "$OUT/metadata/openplanner-revision.txt"
           pnpm -C .sandbox-deps/openplanner ... install --frozen-lockfile 2>&1 | tee "$OUT/logs/install-openplanner.log"
           pnpm -C .sandbox-deps/openplanner ... run build 2>&1 | tee "$OUT/logs/build-openplanner.log"
-          git -C .sandbox-deps/openplanner rev-parse HEAD > "$OUT/metadata/openplanner-revision.txt"
```
</details>

**The Discord `:after` cursor stops advancing under ordinary channel traffic.**

`next-cursor` advances only when both of these conditions hold:
- `raw-count < limit`.
- `raw-count = (count items)`.

Normal Discord reads break these conditions:
- `normalized-item` drops rows with no text, media, or reactions, for example join or pin system messages. Then `(count items)` is less than `raw-count`.

- If 24 or more messages arrive after the cursor, the page is full. In that case `raw-count = limit`.

After any of these events, `read-request` sends the same `:after` cursor on every tick. The poll returns the same oldest page after that cursor every time. Messages beyond that page are never observed. `prepare-page` treats each poll as a replay, so no error makes the stall visible. In `:after` mode, the source stops observing new messages permanently.

Compute the extrema from all raw row ids, not only from admitted items. Advance to the newest raw id when the read is otherwise proven, including on a full page. Keep `:overflow?` and `:reason` in coverage so the report stays truthful. Rows dropped by design, such as empty rows, should not block the cursor. `86-93`: **🩺 Stability & Availability** | **🔵 Trivial** | **⚡ Quick win** **Stop the prompt after a disclosure refusal.** When `settle-disclosure-refusal!` runs, `finalize-failure!` (`finalize-turn-failure!` in `turn.cljs`) marks the run failed and then rethrows `err`. That rethrow is the only thing that stops `start!` before it reaches `retain-resources!` and `prompt!`. If a future change makes failure finalization return a value instead of throwing, `disclosed` becomes that value. `(:agent-spec disclosed)` is then nil, and the turn prompts the provider on a run that is already settled as failed. Make the stop explicit. Throw after a refusal settles so the guarantee does not depend on how the callback behaves.
Proposed fix ```diff disclosed (if (:refused? published) - (await (settle-disclosure-refusal! finalize-failure! config session params persisted (:memory published))) + (do (await (settle-disclosure-refusal! finalize-failure! config session params persisted (:memory published))) + (throw (ex-info "Character disclosure refused" {:reason :character-disclosure-authority-unavailable}))) (await (final-disclosure-or-refuse! finalize-failure! runtime config session params auth-context persisted (:memory published))))] ```
